rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3-4, Tables 1-3, Fig. 5 - the authors process 8 PlanetScope surface-reflectance images of a 500 m buffer on the Araguaia River (Jan-Jul 2018), classify water by NDVI < 0.15, and regress flood area against in-situ gauge discharge/level and JASON-2 altimetry, reporting R2 = 96.49% (flow), 94.38% (level), 88.83% (altimetry), with RMSE 717.59 m3/s and SD 553.63 m3/s for flow.
rows.notes: The study's own result is a proof-of-concept that CubeSat-derived flood area can estimate river discharge and water level at one virtual station on one river over seven months (8 images). It does not report any result on water conservation or on water being managed more efficiently; the link to sub-basin discharge monitoring and improved water management in developing countries appears only as a recommendation in the abstract, discussion and conclusion. The study therefore supports only a precondition (a flow-estimation tool) of the effect claimed under the water_conservation function, so Q2 is answered no and upstream is set. Had the flow-estimation part alone been the claim, the study offers validation against two independent references (in-situ gauge and satellite altimetry), measures the intermediate variable (flooded area), states a buffer-width condition (0.5-1 times river width), notes limitations (only 8 cloud-free images, no SWIR bands, poorer accuracy at high discharge when level rises within the channel), and reports SD of residuals; but it covers a single site/reach and a single season.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Single-site methodological testbed study on the Araguaia River, Brazil; no agricultural water-use or conservation outcomes are measured.
